children: Sweden’s household confidence indicator rose to 98 in August 2026 from an upwardly revised 97.2 in the previous month.

It marked the highest reading since November 2024, as households’ assessment of the economy over the past 12 months improved (-15 vs -19 in July), as well as their expectations for the coming year (-3 vs -8).
Views on personal finances remained stable, with assessments of the past 12 months unchanged (4) and expectations for the next 12 months holding steady (9).
Moreover, labor market concerns eased, with expectations for unemployment over the next year falling (17 vs 22), while perceptions of the risk of becoming unemployed improved slightly (-1 vs -2).
Meanwhile, saving intentions remained unchanged (49), and plans to purchases capital goods became less negative (-12 vs -13).
Households estimated current inflation at 9.2% in August from 9.3% in the previous month, while the expected inflation over the next 12 months slightly eased to 6.8% from 6.9%.

title: Sweden Consumer Morale at 21-Month High
